findings.description: `electLeader()` sends `layoutask` only once when it has no usable kept layout, with no retry or acknowledgement if the request or its answer is lost. When a late old-time-keeper layout has cleared the cached new layout, either dropped broadcast leaves the device using the old joins until an unrelated presence update or layout broadcast occurs.
findings.title: A dropped request leaves stale joins in place

citations.citation:
**Where data gets lost today and what handles it**
| Layer | Loses data? | Handled by |
|---|---|---|
| One WebRTC link | Packets drop. Data channels are reliable and ordered: SCTP resends only the missing parts (selective acknowledgements) | The browser |
| The relay | Yes. Supabase broadcasts have no acknowledgement and can be dropped under load | `need`: the receiver lists the missing pieces every 1.5 s and only those are sent again |
| A holder going away | Yes: a phone locks, leaves or goes slow | Today: the transfer asks the same device again and gives up after a minute (C12). Later: R2 |

evidence.explanation: The election branch sends one request, and receiving the current leader's layout is the only shown path that installs its joins. Room messages use Supabase broadcasts, which the architecture states have no acknowledgement and can be dropped under load; neither the new request nor its answer has a retry path.

findings.description: The `layout` handler clears `earlyLayouts` whenever a message names the device it still considers time keeper, even if it has already cached a layout from the successor. If that older time keeper’s broadcast arrives after the successor’s layout but before the delayed presence update, `electLeader()` finds nothing to adopt; joins between devices still present can remain stale because the successor is not asked to resend.
findings.title: Late devices can lose the new layout

evidence.explanation: The new handler caches a valid non-leader layout but clears that cache on any valid layout attributed to the locally recognized leader. Election consumes only what remains in the cache; presence sync merely filters joins involving departed devices, and only the leader sends a layout on sync. The new handover test covers a successor broadcast before the delayed presence update, but not an intervening old-leader broadcast.
